# OpenAI will remove GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini from the API on January 14, 2027, recommending gpt-6-luna

OpenAI Verified @OpenAI

On Oct 14 OpenAI's API deprecations page announced that GPT-4o (2024-08-06 and 2024-11-20 snapshots), GPT-4o mini (2024-07-18), GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini (2025-04-14) will be removed from the API on January 14, 2027. Fine-tunes built on them shut down the same day, and the recommended replacement for all four is gpt-6-luna, listed at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per 1M tokens versus $2.50 / $10 for GPT-4o.

## Key Takeaways

- ✓ Shutdown: January 14, 2027 (about 3 months' notice) for gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4o-2024-11-20, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 and gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14
- ✓ Fine-tuned versions follow the base model's shutdown date; existing customers already lose new fine-tuning jobs on Jan 6, 2027
- ✓ Standard price per 1M tokens (input/output): gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50, GPT-4o $2.50/$10, GPT-4.1 $2.00/$8.00, GPT-4.1 mini $0.40/$1.60, GPT-4o mini $0.15/$0.60
- ✓ Monitor programmatically via the shutdown_date field on GET /v1/models
- ✓ Second October deprecation wave: older snapshots such as gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and o4-mini shut down Oct 23; gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5.1 go on Apr 1, 2027

🖼️ Official Media

OpenAI API pricing developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

## In-Depth Technical Analysis

OpenAI's API deprecations page (Oct 14, 2026) lists GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4o-2024-11-20), GPT-4o mini (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18), GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini (2025-04-14 snapshots) for removal on January 14, 2027, with gpt-6-luna as the recommended replacement for all of them. Fine-tuned versions follow the same schedule, and existing customers lose the ability to create new fine-tuning jobs on Jan 6, 2027, so teams relying on 4o/4.1 fine-tunes need a retraining plan now. OpenAI publishes no quality comparison between gpt-6-luna and GPT-4o, so run regression evals on real traffic, especially structured outputs and tool calls. On price the move is a large cut: standard rates are $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens for gpt-6-luna versus $2.50/$10 for GPT-4o and $2.00/$8.00 for GPT-4.1. Use the shutdown_date field on GET /v1/models to alert on deprecations automatically.

GPT-4o API Shutdown: January 14, 2027, Move to Luna | CellCog

# GPT-4o API Shutdown: January 14, 2027, Move to Luna

 Nitish Garg · Founder & CEO, CellCog · 14 October 2026 · 5 min read · 934 words 

At a glance Quick answers

When does GPT-4o stop working in the API?
: January 14, 2027, for gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and gpt-4o-2024-11-20, per OpenAI’s deprecations page.
What should I migrate to?
: OpenAI names gpt-6-luna as the replacement for GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini.
Is this about ChatGPT?
: No. The October 14 notice covers the API; the deprecations page does not mention ChatGPT.

Fig 0 GPT-4o's API shutdown date and its replacement, from OpenAI's own pages. Made by CellCog's image agent, running GPT Image 2.5.

OpenAI is retiring GPT-4o from its API on January 14, 2027. On October 14, 2026, it notified developers that GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini are deprecated, per its deprecations page. The named replacement for all four is GPT-6 Luna.

If an app or pipeline still calls one of these models, it has three months to move. Here is what changes, what the replacement costs, and what to check first.

On this page · 6 sections Open

1. What OpenAI announced
2. The notice is shorter than OpenAI’s usual
3. What the replacement costs
4. What to test before you switch
5. What we are watching
6. Sources

Key points 5 · 5 min full read

1. OpenAI notified developers on October 14, 2026 that four GPT-4 series models leave the API on January 14, 2027.
2. The four: GPT-4o (two snapshots), GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini; fine-tuned versions follow the same schedule.
3. OpenAI names one replacement for all four: gpt-6-luna.
4. On OpenAI’s model pages, GPT-6 Luna lists $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens, against $2.50 and $10 for GPT-4o.
5. The notice runs three months; OpenAI’s own policy promises generally available models at least six, with an exception for safety or compliance.

## § 01 What OpenAI announced#

The notice is short: “On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.”

| Model | Snapshots | Shutdown | Replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-4o | gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 | January 14, 2027 | gpt-6-luna |
| GPT-4o mini | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | January 14, 2027 | gpt-6-luna |
| GPT-4.1 | gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 | January 14, 2027 | gpt-6-luna |
| GPT-4.1 mini | gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 | January 14, 2027 | gpt-6-luna |

Table 1 The October 14 deprecation (OpenAI deprecations page, read October 14, 2026)

One line matters most for teams that trained their own versions: “Fine-tuned versions of these models follow the same shutdown schedule as their underlying base models.” A fine-tune on GPT-4o stops on the same day as GPT-4o.

## § 02 The notice is shorter than OpenAI’s usual#

OpenAI’s own policy, on the same page, sets the notice it aims to give: at least six months for generally available models. This notice runs three months, from October 14 to January 14.

The page gives no reason. The policy does carry an exception: “If safety or compliance concerns require us to retire a model sooner, we will provide as much notice as reasonably possible.” We could not find a statement from OpenAI tying this notice to that clause, so we read it only as a shorter window than the policy’s default.

For teams that cannot move in time, OpenAI says “In some cases, developers may be able to provision dedicated capacity for continued access after a model’s shutdown date,” through its sales team.

## § 03 What the replacement costs#

On price, the move goes in the developer’s favor. These are the list prices on OpenAI’s model pages for GPT-6 Luna, GPT-4o and GPT-4.1, per million tokens.

| Model | Input | Cached input | Output | Context window | Max output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-4o | $2.50 | $1.25 | $10.00 | 128,000 | 16,384 |
| GPT-4o mini | $0.15 | $0.075 | $0.60

OpenAI sets a January 2027 shutdown date for five GPT-4 models · Azeem Hassni

# OpenAI sets a January 2027 shutdown date for five GPT-4 models 

Five GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 model IDs stop working in the API on 14 January 2027, with gpt-6-luna named as the replacement.

 13 October 2026 Source: OpenAI 

OpenAI’s API deprecations page now lists five GPT-4 series models for removal on 14 January 2027: `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` and `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`. The page states that developers using these models were notified of the deprecation today, 14 October, giving exactly three months’ notice.

Fine-tuned models built on top of any of these five follow the same shutdown date as their base model. OpenAI names `gpt-6-luna` as the recommended replacement across the board.

```
gpt-4o-2024-08-06       -> gpt-6-luna
gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18  -> gpt-6-luna
```

Why it matters: `gpt-4o` and `gpt-4o-mini` are still some of the most commonly hardcoded model strings out there, in scripts, SDKs and config files that haven’t been touched since 2024. If you’ve got either pinned anywhere, including inside a fine-tuned model, this is the deadline to put in your calendar and the point to start testing `gpt-6-luna` as a drop-in replacement rather than waiting until January.

Written by

Azeem Hassni

# OpenAI is retiring GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 API snapshots: migrate without regressions

A source-led production migration plan for the GPT-4-series API shutdown, covering exact model inventory, compatibility evidence, fine-tuned routes and reversible rollout.

Noor Yasser 14 October 2026 9 min read

An editorial interpretation of the topic, followed by a practical execution diagram.

ON THIS PAGE

OpenAI announced on 14 October 2026 that five dated GPT-4-series API snapshots will be removed on 14 January 2027: two GPT-4o snapshots, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini. OpenAI recommends GPT-6 Luna for all five. The practical response is not a one-line model-name replacement: inventory every production route, freeze a representative test set, version the complete request contract, compare outputs and tool behavior, then ship through shadow traffic and a reversible canary. This matters to teams running structured extraction, tool calling, customer support, content workflows or fine-tuned GPT-4 descendants—especially because fine-tuned versions inherit the same shutdown date.

The official OpenAI deprecations page is the source of record for the announcement and dates. It lists `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` and `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14` for shutdown on 14 January 2027, with `gpt-6-luna` as the recommended replacement. Those model IDs, dates and replacement are documented facts. The testing, routing and rollout plan below is engineering analysis for reducing migration risk; OpenAI has not claimed that every application will behave identically after changing the model.

## What exactly is being retired

The notice targets explicit dated snapshots, not an abstract product family. That distinction matters because production systems often hide model IDs behind aliases, environment variables, prompt-management tools, SDK defaults, batch jobs, fine-tuning job outputs or a vendor gateway. Search configuration, code, observability dimensions and deployment manifests for the exact IDs. Also inspect stored request templates and scheduled workers that may run less often than the main API path.

Build one inventory row per route: owner, endpoint, model ID, snapshot or fine-tuned model, prompt version, schema version, tools, traffic, data class, latency SLO, fallback, last successful request and removal deadline. Treat an unresolved row as operational debt. A dashboard showing only the visible model name is insufficient if the actual request is rewritten by a gateway.

Fine-tuned models need a separate branch in the plan. OpenAI states that fine-tuned versions of the listed models follow the same shutdown schedule as their base models. The GPT-6 Luna model page currently marks fine-tuning as unsupported. Therefore, do not assume that an existing fine-tuned model can be recreated directly on Luna. Recover the original training and validation data, document the behavior the fine-tune supplied, test whether prompting, retrieval or deterministic code can replace it, and choose another supported path only after verifying current official documentation.

## The migration unit is the request contract

Changing only `model` ignores the parts most likely to cause regressions. Version the model together with instructions, message roles, reasoning effort, tool definitions, JSON Schema, response parser, retry policy, timeouts, safety checks, conversation-state strategy and cost or latency budgets. A release should point to one immutable contract bundle so the old and new paths can be replayed and compared.

The GPT-6 Luna documentation describes a 1.05-million-token context window, 128,000 maximum output tokens, text and image input, Structured Outputs, function calling and reasoning-effort controls. It also says built-in tools and function calling use the Responses API, while Chat Completions supports function calling only when reasoning effort is `none`. The

Built on GPT-4o? OpenAI Switches It Off on January 14, 2027, and the Replacement Costs 20x Less

# Built on GPT-4o? OpenAI Switches It Off on January 14, 2027, and the Replacement Costs 20x Less

Origami Team Editorial Team

October 14, 2026

Like what we publish? Pin Origami as a preferred source on Google.

## Built on GPT-4o? OpenAI Switches It Off on January 14, 2027, and the Replacement Costs 20x Less

On October 14, 2026, OpenAI announced that five GPT-4 family models will be shut down in its API on January 14, 2027: both versions of GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini. Any chatbot, invoicing tool or message-sorting system a developer built for you on one of these models will stop answering that day unless it is moved first. OpenAI's recommended replacement is GPT-6 Luna, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, against $2.50 and $10 for GPT-4o, roughly 20 to 25 times cheaper. You have 92 days: audit your systems this week, test the replacement on your own data, and switch before mid-December.

### What exactly OpenAI announced

OpenAI published the notice on its developer deprecations page. It lists the following model IDs, all shutting down on January 14, 2027:

- gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and gpt-4o-2024-11-20 (GPT-4o)
- gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 (the small model many systems were built on because it was cheap)
- gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 and gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14

The page states that fine-tuned versions of these models follow the same shutdown date as their base model. The notice covers the API, meaning systems built by developers, not the ChatGPT app your staff use in the browser.

### An earlier deadline: October 23, 2026

The same page carries an older notice, issued on April 22, 2026, that shuts down older models just 9 days from today, on October 23, 2026. They include the first GPT-4o snapshot gpt-4o-2024-05-13, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, o1, o3-mini and o4-mini. If your system is old and has not been updated in two years, it may run on one of these, and that is worth a call to your developer today, not next month.

### How your bill changes: a worked example

Prices below come from OpenAI's pricing page, in US dollars per million tokens (a token is roughly part of a word):

| Model | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-4o | $2.50 | $10.00 |
| GPT-4.1 | $2.00 | $8.00 |
| GPT-4.1 mini | $0.40 | $1.60 |
| GPT-4o mini | $0.15 | $0.60 |
| GPT-6 Luna (replacement) | $0.10 | $0.50 |

A hypothetical example for illustration: a customer service chatbot handling 20,000 conversations a month, each with about 3,000 input tokens and 500 output tokens. On GPT-4o it costs about $250 a month (around SAR 937 at 3.75), and on GPT-6 Luna about $11 (around SAR 41). If it runs on GPT-4o mini the gap is smaller: about $15 against $11. Note that Luna is a reasoning model with a default effort of medium, and that reasoning is billed as output tokens; set it to none or low for simple tasks, or the bill will come in above this example.

### What can break when you switch

- Fine-tuned models: according to the GPT-6 Luna model page, it does not support fine-tuning. If your system depends on a fine-tuned GPT-4o, there is no ready equivalent, and you will need sharper instructions and examples instead, or another model.
- Tool calls: the same page says function calling through Chat Completions works with Luna only when reasoning effort is set to none. A system that connects AI to your inventory or booking system may stop carrying out actions if this is not set.
- Assistants API: Luna does not run on the Assistants or Realtime endpoints, so systems built on them need partial rebuilding, not just a new model name.
- Factual accuracy: in our earlier comparison Claude Haiku 5.5 vs GPT-6 Luna we cited Artificial Analysis testing showing that Luna often gets things wrong when answering from memory. If your chatbot answers questions about your prices and policies, give it the information in e

# OpenAI Will Shut Off GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 in the API on January 14, 2027, Giving Developers 3 Months When Its Policy Promises 6

OpenAI told developers on 14 Oct 2026 that GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini leave the API on 14 Jan 2027, fine-tunes included. GPT-6 Luna is the named replacement and is cheaper per token, but the 92-day notice is half what OpenAI's own policy promises.

 By Abhinav Ramaswamy October 14, 2026 8 min read 

OpenAI told developers on October 14, 2026 that GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini will be removed from its API on January 14, 2027. Fine-tuned versions of those models go dark on the same day. The notice sits at the top of OpenAI’s API deprecations page, and the recommended replacement for all four is a single model: `gpt-6-luna`.

That gives teams 92 days. The same OpenAI page says generally available models get “at least 6 months” of notice unless safety or compliance concerns require a faster timeline. The October 14 entry gives no reason for the shorter window.

For most apps the move will lower the bill on paper. For anyone running a fine-tuned GPT-4o or GPT-4.1, or leaning on non-reasoning speed, it is a real migration project with a hard date.

## Exactly what OpenAI is shutting down

The deprecation table lists dated snapshots, not bare model names. Here is the full list from OpenAI’s notice.

| Model | Snapshot IDs being removed | Shutdown date | Recommended replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-4o | `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20` | January 14, 2027 | `gpt-6-luna` |
| GPT-4o mini | `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` | January 14, 2027 | `gpt-6-luna` |
| GPT-4.1 | `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` | January 14, 2027 | `gpt-6-luna` |
| GPT-4.1 mini | `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14` | January 14, 2027 | `gpt-6-luna` |

One detail matters if your code just says `gpt-4o`. OpenAI’s GPT-4o model page says that alias points to `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, one of the snapshots on the list. The GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini aliases also point to listed snapshots. The notice does not spell out what the bare names will do after January 14, so the safe plan is to treat them as going away too.

The oldest GPT-4o snapshot, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, is not part of this notice because it already has an earlier date. It shuts down on October 23, 2026, nine days from now, along with `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `o3-mini` and `o4-mini`.

## Is GPT-6 Luna a fair swap? The price math

On list price, yes. OpenAI’s pricing page puts every retiring model above Luna on both input and output.

| Model (Standard tier) | Input / 1M tokens | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-4o | $2.50 | $1.25 | $10.00 |
| GPT-4.1 | $2.00 | $0.50 | $8.00 |
| GPT-4.1 mini | $0.40 | $0.10 | $1.60 |
| GPT-4o mini | $0.15 | $0.075 | $0.60 |
| GPT-6 Luna | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 |

Take a support bot that reads 50 million tokens and writes 10 million a month. On GPT-4o that is about $225. On GPT-4.1 it is about $180. On Luna, with the same output, it is about $10.

The catch is that Luna is a reasoning model and the old ones are not. The Luna model page lists reasoning effort settings from `none` to `max`, with `medium` as the default. OpenAI’s reasoning guide says reasoning tokens are billed as output tokens.

That matters most for GPT-4o mini users. The same 50 million in, 10 million out workload costs about $13.50 on GPT-4o mini. If Luna’s default reasoning adds another 10 million output tokens, the Luna bill rises to about $15, slightly more than what you pay today. Set the effort level on purpose instead of taking the default.

Two more pricing rules to check. Luna bills cache writes at 1.25 times the input rate, and prompts over 272,000 input tokens cost 2 times on input and 1.5 times on output for the whole request. GPT-4.1 users who feed in very long docu

# Your OpenAI model IDs stop on 23 October, so map each one before then

D Dave Author

Oct 13, 2026· 6 min read

Your app can keep calling a model ID that OpenAI stops serving on 23 October 2026. OpenAI's deprecations page lists a replacement for each one, and most of the table shares that single date.

## What the OpenAI page says Copy Anchor Link

The page has a section headed "2026-04-22: Legacy GPT model snapshots." It lists each snapshot with a shutdown date of October 23, 2026 and a substitute model. The page does not say that requests will fail. It says: "At the time of the shut down, the model or endpoint will no longer be accessible." A call to a model that is no longer accessible cannot succeed, so treat the date as the end of that ID.

The page also has a separate section for April 2027. It says: "The following models are deprecated and will be removed from the API on April 1, 2027, with six months' notice." That list names GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.4-Nano, and it is not part of this October deadline. If you want that one, read the April 2027 migration checklist.

The rules below are ours, and they are labelled as ours.

## The snapshots that stop on 23 October Copy Anchor Link

The table below is taken from the page. Where the page lists an alias next to a snapshot, the alias is in brackets. Fine-tuned models have their own table, which names a recommended base model rather than a direct replacement.

| Model ID | Replacement on the page | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-3.5-turbo-0125` (`gpt-3.5-turbo`) | `gpt-5.6-terra` | Alias listed too |
| `gpt-4-0613` (`gpt-4`) | `gpt-5.6-sol` | Alias listed too |
| `gpt-4-1106-preview` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | |
| `gpt-4-turbo` (`gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09`) | `gpt-5.6-sol` | |
| `gpt-4.1-nano` (`gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`) | `gpt-5.6-luna` | |
| `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | |
| `gpt-image-1` | `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Image model, two options listed |
| `o1` (`o1-2024-12-17`) | `gpt-5.6-sol` | |
| `o1-pro` (`o1-pro-2025-03-19`) | `gpt-5.6-sol` with `reasoning.mode: pro` | The page lists the mode setting |
| `o3-mini` (`o3-mini-2025-01-31`) | `gpt-5.6-sol` | |
| `o4-mini` (`o4-mini-2025-04-16`) | `gpt-5.6-terra` | |
| `ft-o4-mini-2025-04-16` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | Fine-tuned snapshot |

The fine-tuned table lists five more: `ft-gpt-3.5-turbo` and `ft-babbage-002` and `ft-davinci-002` take `gpt-5.6-terra` as the base model, `ft-gpt-4` takes `gpt-5.6-sol`, and `ft-gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14` takes `gpt-5.6-luna`. The table names a base model for each one, so a fine-tuned app means retraining on that base. Your training data and the new base model are a separate job.

The SaaS Dashboard Kit includes login, a database, and a working dashboard. Live demo at saas.otf-kit.dev.

## Find every ID in your code Copy Anchor Link

Search the repository for the model strings in the table above, and search for the aliases too. A string like `gpt-4` can match more than one place, so read each hit. Check the environment files, the CI secrets, the admin settings and any prompt store you keep outside the repo, because a model ID often lives in one of those and not in the code.

Keep the IDs in one config file. Our rule is one place per model choice, so a switch touches one line rather than a dozen call sites. The map can be as small as this:

Copy Text

```
// model choices, in one place
export const MODELS = {
  chat: "gpt-5.6-sol",
  cheap: "gpt-5.6-luna",
} as const
```

Name the purpose, not the model. A name like `chat` survives the next migration, and a name like `gpt4` does not.

# GPT-4o retirement in 2026: the ChatGPT dates and the separate API story

GPT-4o left ChatGPT on February 13, 2026, but the API is a separate story: base gpt-4o shows no shutdown, while gpt-4o-2024-05-13 ends on October 23, 2026.

By Manu Lopes 8 min read

Published September 27, 2026 at 12:03 Updated October 11, 2026 at 02:08

Conceptual illustration of separate ChatGPT and API timelines; no real interface shown.

In this article

GPT-4o is an OpenAI language model that people meet in two different places: the model picker in ChatGPT, and the `gpt-4o` model ID that applications send to the OpenAI API. According to OpenAI's announcement, GPT-4o left ChatGPT on February 13, 2026. The API followed a separate path.

On October 11, 2026, OpenAI's API deprecations page does not list the base `gpt-4o` model for shutdown. It does list one dated snapshot, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, for shutdown on October 23, 2026. An administrator should care because "GPT-4o is retired" is true for ChatGPT users and misleading for developers, and the dates that matter differ for each group.

## In short

- OpenAI announced on January 29, 2026 that GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini and o4-mini would leave ChatGPT on February 13, 2026.
- ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu customers kept GPT-4o inside custom GPTs until April 3, 2026. After that date it was retired on all plans.
- The API alias `chatgpt-4o-latest` was announced for removal on November 18, 2025 and shut down on February 17, 2026.
- The API snapshot `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` was announced on April 22, 2026 and is scheduled to shut down on October 23, 2026.
- The base `gpt-4o` and `gpt-4o-mini` model pages show no deprecation notice. Audio, realtime and transcription variants have their own, later dates.

Verification status. The two OpenAI pages that carry the ChatGPT dates, the Help Center article and the announcement, returned HTTP 403 to our fetch tool. We read them only through search-result summaries. The ChatGPT dates above are therefore not verified from the pages themselves. The API facts come from pages we fetched directly on October 11, 2026.

## How it works

Think of three layers. The first is the ChatGPT product: a model picker, saved conversations, projects and custom GPTs. OpenAI controls which models appear there, and a retirement removes the choice for everyone on the plan.

The second layer is the API, where an application names a model ID in each request. An ID can be an alias that moves over time or a dated snapshot that stays fixed. `chatgpt-4o-latest` was an alias. Its model page says it pointed to the GPT-4o snapshot used in ChatGPT, and that it has been deprecated and removed from the API. The changelog says it became a dynamic model on August 15, 2024.

The third layer is the variant. GPT-4o also powers audio, realtime, transcription and search-preview models. Each has its own entry and date on the deprecations page.

OpenAI uses two terms. Per the deprecations page, a deprecation is the process of retiring a model, and a shutdown (also called sunset) is the point where it is no longer accessible. The page states notice periods: at least 6 months for generally available models, at least 3 months for specialized variants, and as little as 2 weeks for preview models. It adds that safety or compliance concerns can shorten these periods.

The table below combines both layers. It reflects what we read on October 11, 2026.

| ChatGPT conversations | GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, o4-mini | Retired | February 13, 2026 | Search summary of OpenAI pages |

| API alias | `chatgpt-4o-latest` | Shut down | February 17, 2026 | Deprecations page, model page |

# GPT-4 shutdown on 23 October: the migration map

The GPT-4 shutdown hits on 23 October 2026. OpenAI's full old-to-new model table, the price change for each move, and the gotchas that break silently.

The GPT-4 shutdown lands on 23 October 2026, 32 days from today. On that date OpenAI removes `gpt-4`, `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3-mini`, `o4-mini`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `gpt-image-1` and five families of fine-tuned models from the API. Below is OpenAI's full substitute table, what each move does to your per-token price, and the behaviour changes that break quietly.

- Shutdown date: 23 October 2026, announced on 22 April 2026.
- What happens: at shutdown a model is no longer accessible, so requests naming it stop working.
- Who is affected: any code, config or fine-tuned model that sends one of the IDs below.
- Sooner still:`gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`, `babbage-002` and `davinci-002` shut down on 28 September 2026, with `gpt-5.6-terra` as the substitute.

## The GPT-4 shutdown migration map, model by model

This is the table from OpenAI's deprecations page, reproduced as published. Where a row shows a pipe, the first ID is the snapshot and the IDs after it are aliases that go with it.

| Shutdown date | Model snapshot | Substitute model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-3.5-turbo-0125` | `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-completions` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-4-0613` | `gpt-4`, `gpt-4-0613-completions`, `gpt-4-completions` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-4-1106-preview` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-4-turbo` | `gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09`, `gpt-4-turbo-completions` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-4.1-nano` | `gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14` | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `gpt-image-1` | `gpt-image-2` |
| October 23, 2026 | `o1-2024-12-17` | `o1` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `o1-pro-2025-03-19` | `o1-pro` | `gpt-5.6-sol` (`reasoning.mode: pro`) |
| October 23, 2026 | `o3-mini-2025-01-31` | `o3-mini` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-o4-mini-2025-04-16` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| October 23, 2026 | `o4-mini-2025-04-16` | `o4-mini` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |

OpenAI is also removing fine-tuned versions on the same date:

| Shutdown date | Model snapshot | Recommended replacement base model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-gpt-3.5-turbo` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-gpt-4` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14` | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-babbage-002` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| October 23, 2026 | `ft-davinci-002` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |

Two readings of this table matter. First, the alias does not save you: `gpt-4` and the `gpt-4-0613` snapshot go together. Second, nothing here is a like-for-like swap. Every text substitute is a GPT-5.6 reasoning model, and several of the models they replace, including `gpt-4` and `gpt-3.5-turbo`, were not.

## What each move does to your price

Here are the Standard per-million-token prices from OpenAI's pricing page for every row where both the old and new model are listed. Output tokens on the new models include reasoning tokens, which is the subject of the next section.

# OpenAI API shuts down 12 legacy models on Oct 23: o4-mini, o3-mini, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and gpt-image-1 included, 12 days left to migrate

OpenAI Verified @OpenAI

Per OpenAI's official Deprecations page, a batch of legacy snapshots deprecated on Apr 22 stops serving in the API on Oct 23, 2026: 12 snapshots and their aliases including gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-2024-05-13, gpt-image-1, o1, o1-pro, o3-mini and o4-mini, plus five fine-tuned model families. Official substitutes are gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna and gpt-image-2.5. The #keep4o campaign to preserve GPT-4o snapshots resurfaced on X today.

## Key Takeaways

- ✓ 12 snapshots plus aliases go dark together: `o4-mini`, `o3-mini`, `o1`, `o1-pro`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-3.5-turbo` aliases stop resolving (OpenAI Deprecations)
- ✓ Shutdown date Oct 23, 2026 — 12 days away; announced Apr 22, meeting OpenAI's 6-month minimum for GA models
- ✓ Substitutes: o4-mini / gpt-3.5 → `gpt-5.6-terra`; gpt-4 family / o1 / o3-mini / gpt-4o-2024-05-13 → `gpt-5.6-sol`; o1-pro → `gpt-5.6-sol` with `reasoning.mode: pro`; gpt-4.1-nano → `gpt-5.6-luna`
- ✓`gpt-image-1` → `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `-flare`; five fine-tuned families (`ft-gpt-4`, `ft-gpt-3.5-turbo`, `ft-o4-mini`, etc.) also shut down and must be retrained on new bases
- ✓ Next wave: Dec 1 (gpt-image-1.5 / 1-mini) and Dec 11 (first-gen gpt-5 snapshots, o3, o3-pro)

### Key Decision Metrics at a Glance

## In-Depth Technical Analysis

OpenAI's Deprecations page confirms that the batch of legacy snapshots announced on Apr 22, 2026 stops serving in the API on Oct 23, 2026. Affected: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-2024-05-13, gpt-image-1, o1-2024-12-17, o1-pro-2025-03-19, o3-mini-2025-01-31, o4-mini-2025-04-16 and ft-o4-mini, plus their aliases (o1, o1-pro, o3-mini, o4-mini, gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo), and fine-tuned ft-gpt-3.5-turbo, ft-gpt-4, ft-gpt-4.1-nano, ft-babbage-002 and ft-davinci-002. Substitutes: gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-4 family, o1, o3-mini, gpt-4o; o1-pro via reasoning.mode: pro), gpt-5.6-terra (o4-mini, gpt-3.5), gpt-5.6-luna (gpt-4.1-nano), and gpt-image-2.5-sunburst/flare for gpt-image-1. OpenAI published no head-to-head benchmarks or price comparisons in the notice, so replay your own production samples before switching. Grep code, env vars and prompt-management configs for these IDs, retrain fine-tunes on new bases, and plan for the next waves on Dec 1 (gpt-image-1.5/1-mini) and Dec 11 (first-gen gpt-5 snapshots, o3, o3-pro). The #keep4o campaign asking OpenAI to preserve GPT-4o snapshots trended on X today, but the official shutdown date is unchanged.

Up Next OpenAI will remove GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini from the API on January 14, 2027, recommending gpt-6-luna
